raw_case_text:
Patient information: an 87-year-old Nigerian businessman presented to the eye clinic with a 3-week history of right orbital swelling. He divided his time between the United Kingdom and rural Nigeria. He had longstanding myeloma with previous bone marrow transplant in 2002 and had been on thalidomide derivative therapy for many years. He also had a background of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and well controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
Clinical findings: on examination, he had slightly reduced visual acuities (6/12 right eye, 6/9 left eye) with no relative afferent pupillary defect, and known deuteranomaly. The right eyelid was very swollen and erythematous; his lids had to be pulled open for examination (Figure 1). There appeared to be proptosis, significant conjunctival chemosis, and restricted eye movements. Anterior segment and fundoscopy examination were unremarkable. He was apyrexic and was noted to have weight loss at a routine oncology appointment.
Timeline of current episode: initial diagnosis was presumed orbital cellulitis; this did not respond to antibiotics started in primary care. He subsequently underwent further investigations on hospital admission.
Diagnostic assessment: full blood count showed anemia with thrombocytopenia, inflammatory markers were elevated (CRP 43mg/L). Computerized tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan revealed a retro-orbital mass closely associated with the right lacrimal gland (Figure 2). Nasal endoscopy revealed a healthy right cavity with evidence of mucopus from the left middle meatus, consistent with his CT findings of left maxillary sinusitis.
Diagnosis: he underwent an orbital biopsy revealing fungal hyphae with septation surrounded by chronic granulomatous inflammation, suggesting aspergillus species infection (Figure 3).
Therapeutic interventions: he received 10 days of intravenous (IV) amphotericin B, then switched to IV then oral voriconazole.
Follow-up and outcome of interventions: a repeat scan a month later showed an improvement in proptosis and slightly less bulky aspergilloma. He could not have contrast due to poor renal function. The MRI and CT scans were discussed at our local radiology meeting, and it was thought the orbital mass was communicating with the right frontal sinus (although there was only mild opacification). He developed deranged liver function tests as well as experiencing nightmares on voriconazole and this was discontinued after 6 weeks of treatment. A lower dose of voriconazole was restarted to avoid renal toxicity.
Patient perspective: the patient was initially anxious as he was unsure whether the swelling was related to his multiple myeloma. Once the swelling subsided, he felt reassured that his vision was unchanged. The treatment was the most challenging element, as he found the nightmares caused by the medication highly distressing, and was very happy when the course of antifungal medication was completed. To date, he has had no further recurrences.
Informed consent: yes, consent given to use images for educational purposes only (e.g. teaching, publications) and that all images will be cropped to only show the area of interest.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 87-year-old Nigerian man with multiple myeloma presented with a 3-week history of progressive, antibiotic-refractory right orbital and eyelid swelling and weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the eye clinic with 3 weeks of severe right eyelid and orbital swelling initially treated in primary care with oral antibiotics for presumed preseptal/orbital cellulitis without improvement.
subjective.past_medical_history: Longstanding multiple myeloma status post bone marrow transplantation in 2002, maintained on chronic thalidomide-derivative therapy; chronic kidney disease; well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus; congenital deuteranomaly; businessman dividing his time between the UK and rural Nigeria.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right orbital/eyelid swelling and recent weight loss; afebrile.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile; visual acuity was 6/12 in the right eye and 6/9 in the left eye with no relative afferent pupillary defect and stable color vision (baseline deuteranomaly). Right ocular exam showed severe right upper/lower eyelid edema and erythema (requiring manual lid retraction to examine the globe), right proptosis, marked conjunctival chemosis, and restricted extraocular motility, with normal anterior segment and fundoscopy. Nasal endoscopy showed a healthy right nasal cavity and mucopus in the left middle meatus.
objective.routine_investigations: Full blood count showed anemia and thrombocytopenia, and CRP was elevated at 43 mg/L. During subsequent voriconazole therapy, liver function tests became deranged.
objective.advanced_workup: Non-contrast orbital/sinus CT and MRI (contrast withheld due to chronic kidney disease) demonstrated a right retro-orbital mass closely contiguous with the right lacrimal gland and communicating with a mildly opacified right frontal sinus (plus incidental left maxillary sinusitis). Right orbital biopsy histopathology revealed septate fungal hyphae surrounded by chronic granulomatous inflammation consistent with Aspergillus species.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Right retro-orbital and lacrimal gland granulomatous aspergilloma/invasive orbital aspergillosis (extending from the right frontal sinus) in an immunocompromised patient with multiple myeloma on thalidomide-derivative therapy, confirmed by orbital MRI/CT and orbital biopsy histopathology showing septate fungal hyphae within chronic granulomatous inflammation. Treated with 10 days of intravenous amphotericin B followed by 6 weeks of intravenous-to-oral voriconazole; after developing deranged liver function tests and distressing voriconazole-induced nightmares at week 6, voriconazole was briefly held and restarted at a reduced dose to avoid amphotericin nephrotoxicity, achieving resolution of proptosis and orbital swelling with preserved vision and no recurrence.
